name: Adrian Bhandari
life: “I still remember a folded complaint saved in my work belt.” People around Studio Boulevard know Adrian by a small Tuesday habit. Adrian waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I put my complaint in my pocket. A young constable came outside later to ask if I still wanted to make it.
appearance: Adrian is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and one cheek that creases before the other. Usually dressed in a narrow-striped sweater with a knotted piece of sail thread on a key ring, Adrian counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
personality: Adrian can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Adrian can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To bring the complaint to the quieter second meeting.
family: Winifred Kerr is Adrian’s stepsibling. Adrian puts the kettle on. Winifred chooses the music. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The crash anniversary*, Winifred says, “I still drive over it because my livelihood depends on the road.”
connections: Vivian Acosta. They arrange two private ways to finish a complaint after the storm.

reactions.situation: An officer asks whether the wet event should still count as a hearing
reactions.response: Adrian asks who missed the chance to speak before calling the hearing complete.

reactions.response: Adrian offers to accompany the caller to a familiar public meeting place without turning speculation into neighborhood news.
